title: No overridable calls from a constructor

blocks.text: The page's best practice: **don't call overridable methods from constructors**. The superclass constructor runs first, before the subclass has set its own fields, so a subclass override called from there sees those fields still `null` (or 0).
Write `Widget` and its nested static subclass `Widget.Button`:

items: `label()` returns `Button:` followed by the current text;
`setText(String text)` changes the text; the label and the summary follow it.

blocks.text:
new Widget("w1").summary()                 -> "Widget#w1"
new Widget.Button("b1", "OK").summary()    -> "Button:OK#b1"
b.setText("Cancel"); b.summary()           -> "Button:Cancel#b1"

cases.says: A widget's summary is its label and id, and a button's label names its text.
A button's summary shows the text the button was created with, not null.
After setText, the button's label and summary show the new text.

concepts: A constructor must not call an overridable method, because the override runs before the subclass's fields are set.
